scope: HIS-06 and DATA-01..05 source/offline verification, not completed product acceptance

observed: Product export supports JSON/JSONL and --sanitize; sanitizer drops the verbatim projection and redacts transcript/file fields. Five actual archive tests preserve parts, round-trip without legacy tables, import V1, map compaction summaries and reject unsupported archive versions.
Native CLI export is a separate committed-events JSONL surface with explicit database/session/cursor.
remaining: The product command only exposes json/jsonl, so the requested full Markdown export is not supplied by that command.
Executed archive tests do not exercise the sanitizer or prove no sensitive fields leak through every part variant.
Current native-archive import/export UX, large-attachment omission notices and unknown-billing/protected-content labeling need explicit acceptance.

observed: The engine serializes schema migration using a filesystem lock and SQLite transaction, distinguishes its application ID, and refuses a schema newer than SCHEMA_VERSION. Concurrent-open tests cover two live processes and concurrent admission, plus recovery respecting a live lease.
Product database tests cover initialization serialization, waiting for running windows during upgrade, peer migration observation and tracked/legacy migration identities.
remaining: These selected tests do not establish interrupted schema-migration recovery across all historical versions.
An end-to-end pre-upgrade backup/verification plus upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade exercise on current release artifacts remains missing.

The native concurrent-open baseline left two child processes after one case; this was reproduced, its own children reaped, and a shared RAII cleanup fix is in PR #1578. That test cleanup issue is not a schema-ownership failure.

observed: Native migration/transfer suites exercise staged/active authority, identity/checksum checks, incompatible or corrupted bundles, exact retries and move into a fresh location.
PRs #1568/#1569/#1573 separately repair freeze completion, implicit model binding and canonical/native history mapping. Their feature regression receipts are distinct from this exact-main baseline.
remaining: The complete current-client TS-to-native/native-workspace/fork/large-attachment matrix is not established.
Move fixes remain open PRs; tests against main do not imply those fixes are merged or released.
The feature intentionally retains non-overwrite rejection when returning to a store already retaining the Session.

observed: The TypeScript product db command retains stats, backfill, vacuum, compact, restore, externalize-blobs, gc-blobs and retention. Destructive compact/GC require flags; backfill/restore/externalization support dry-run, and retention is report-only.
Native standalone CLI has doctor/catalog/export plus serve/ACP, rather than an equivalent db maintenance command family.
remaining: The eight requested maintenance operations are still TS-hosted and have not been migrated to a complete Rust product service/CLI.
Target database/reference/impact presentation and safe dry-run behavior require a command-by-command current-client matrix.
No maintenance was performed on real user databases; the executed tests used fixture databases.

observed: Blob GC scans references conservatively and has a grace window. Tests retain referenced blobs and young orphans, remove unreferenced old blobs, and preserve restore rows.
SessionRetention.plan and the db retention command explicitly report candidates only; deletion remains disabled while history/diff/event readers still need the log.
remaining: Snapshot-then-truncate is not implemented by the report-only retention path.
Native and TS/shared-channel blob reference coverage, bounded per-message rather than per-delta growth, and vacuum/disk-reclamation curves need separate measurement.
Passing the selected GC tests does not prove complete active-native-reference safety or long-running storage bounds.

observed: Native doctor opens the database read-only, checks application/schema identity and SQLite quick_check, reports counts/states, and can run during ownership without reconciling work. Tests reject unrelated, future and missing databases.
Fixture restore tests merge absent sessions/events, advance sequence watermarks, and avoid overwriting existing rows.
remaining: The doctor report does not establish the complete WAL/missing-blob/incomplete-transfer/corrupted-index diagnostic matrix.
An actual backup/restore exercise verifying Session history, attachments, permissions and usage is still required.
Read-only diagnosis is distinct from repair; no repair or user-history deletion was performed.
